title: Mobility analyses of hip fracture patients using artificial intelligence
summary:
Background
Hip fractures are common in older adults. They often lead to reduced mobility and poorer quality of life and can also increase the risk of death. After surgery, many patients are initially only able to move to a limited extent, which can promote complications such as infections, blood clots, or pressure ulcers. So far, there is no suitable and standardized method for continuously and objectively measuring mobility after surgery.

Research Question
The study examines how postoperative movement behavior affects the overall health outcome after hip surgery. The aim is to identify typical movement patterns indicative of poorer recovery. In addition, the study investigates whether complications can be detected earlier and what challenges may arise in collecting mobility data. It also evaluates whether continuous movement measurements can be used to better predict the progression of healing.

Methods
Postoperative mobility is measured for three months using a body-worn sensor. A computer program with artificial intelligence analyzes this data and looks for patterns that may indicate complications or delayed recovery.

interventions.name: Continuous collection of movement data from patients with a hip fracture for up to 2 months after surgery, supplemented by questionnaire-based assessments conducted immediately after surgery, after 5–7 days, and after 6–8 weeks.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a surgically treated pertrochanteric femur fracture or femoral neck fracture
Exclusion criteria:
Severe comorbidities, terminal-stage illnesses, and cognitive impairments (MMSE < 26)
